messages:
alex: Heads up — infra asked to export ~90d of session/auth logs to a partner for vuln triage. They want session IDs and full context. Do we have an approved export lease process and masking rules? cc @maria

maria: We currently limit raw exports to 7d and require SecOps approval. 90d seems out of policy. What exactly do they need from the logs?

sam: Partner says they need full session traces to correlate exploit timeline. We can filter to event classes, but they insist on session_id and some identifiers. That triggers KMS unwrap + extra control.

alex: My proposal: require a temporary export lease via ticket (template below), SecOps + Incident responder approval, DLP scan pass, and automatic audit trail in SIEM. Exports go to an ephemeral encrypted S3 bucket with lifecycle 72h. Redact/hash PII before export.

maria: +1 to ephemeral bucket and DLP. Also ensure exported bundles are deleted after the lease and that KMS grants are timeboxed. Ops should not grant persistent Decrypt rights.

sam: For KMS grants we need a timeboxed principal like export-service role. Example IAM snippet (ops can refine): `Principal: export-service@infra`, `Action: kms:Decrypt`, `Condition: DateLessThan: 2025-11-10T00:00:00Z`

oncall-jane: I can create that timeboxed grant but I need the approved ticket id and justifying text. Also prefer policy: write export to `s3://exports-ephemeral/<ticket>` only, no direct downloads from primary buckets.

security-bot: Incident note: previous export to partner Z lacked redaction and triggered an incident on 2025-11-03 (INC-43). Recommend stricter gating.

maria: That incident is exactly why we should codify RBAC: only SecOps + Infra lead + legal can approve exports that include session-level identifiers. Add a checklist item for legal/contract review.

alex: Drafting a runbook and a small terraform module to formalize this. Draft fields: `kms_grant_duration`, `export_filter`, `dlp_required`, `ephemeral_ttl` — will open PR.

sam: SIEM side: mark any export-related activity with `meta.export_ticket` and `meta.approver`, and create an ingest rule `external_export` so we can trace who accessed the exported bundle. Example log note: `meta.export_ticket: TICKET-2025-847`, `meta.approver: maria`.

maria: Legal also asked that exports pass a DLP scan before being staged. Add DLP results to ticket and deny grant if PII exceeds threshold.

alex: Quick config sketch to include in the PR:
```
export_filter:
  include_events: ["auth","session","alert"]
  redact_fields: ["user.email","user_ip","ssn"]
  dlp_scan: true

kms_grant:
  principal: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/export-service"
  duration: "72h"
  condition: {"StringEquals": {"request:purpose":"forensic-triage"}}

storage:
  s3_bucket: "exports-ephemeral"
  lifecycle_days: 3
```

sam: Also add a terraform IAM template for a timeboxed grant. And an S3 policy that prevents copy-out except to the partner's pre-approved external bucket.

oncall-jane: Creating the ticket now: TICKET-2026-110. I'll provision a temporary CMK grant template and ephemeral bucket. ETA EOD tomorrow for the template. Will attach the ticket here when done.

alex: Thanks. Action items: 1) I will open PR for runbook + tf module, 2) @oncall-jane to create CMK grant template + ephemeral bucket, 3) SecOps (maria) to sign approvals and confirm DLP threshold. We'll update SIEM ingest rules after PR merges.

maria: Sounds good. Please include the approval matrix in the PR (who can approve what).

alex: Will do. pinging everyone once PR is up. :thumbsup:
